reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data through Nov 13: SPX 7,561.67 is 3.61% off its 120-day high, 1.38% below its 50-day and 3.02% above its 200-day; SMH $486.75 is inside Zone 2 ($470-505) and 27.55% off its high; NVDA $162.85 is BELOW Zone 2 ($175-185), 33.09% off its high with RSI 24.9; VIX 19.30 and HY OAS 3.2 are calm; mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4 confirmed.
reaction.invalidation: SPX closes above the $7,750-7,820 failure zone with SMH above $580 and NVDA reclaiming $185 — the correction thesis is void and the stance flips to re-evaluating longs; or HY OAS above 4.0 with VIX above 25, which voids the calm-credit, rotation-not-rollover read entirely.

ladder.response: Stay in Watch. Do not chase the breakdown and do not bottom-fish the next zone down without a new tally print; re-check zone occupancy and tally at the next close.
ladder.trigger: SMH daily close below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or NVDA daily close below $150

ladder.response: Treat it as the trap case: no chasing the first bounce, no new entries on the bounce. Wait for the failure-zone retest verdict before any Tranche A consideration.
ladder.trigger: SMH bounces into the failure zone $580-600 or SPX into $7,750-7,820 and fails there

ladder.response: Stand down. Tranche A and Tranche B stay off, new money stays 100% bills, and the rotation read is void — the regime has broken to risk-off.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4.0 or VIX closes above 25

ladder.response: Tranche A re-arms: deploy 25% per the ladder into Zone 2 names (SMH/NVDA/MU zone prints), sized per the deployment ladder, not all at once.
ladder.trigger: NVDA daily close at or above $175 AND SMH holding $470 AND mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better (VIX rollover or volume climax confirms)

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the live risk: a sharp bounce into the SMH $580-600 / SPX $7,750-7,820 failure zone that fails there would trap first-bounce buyers. Entries therefore wait for the failure-zone retest verdict — a bounce that holds above the failure zone changes the read, a bounce that rejects it confirms the correction and keeps the stance at Watch.

strategyPosture: Watch. The episode is a CORRECTION with the AI complex in or below its buy zones, but no capitulation signal has confirmed and Tranche A is not re-armed (tally 2 of 4, NVDA below its $175 floor). Hold bills, hold the book, let the zone levels and the tally do the work. This week decides it: FOMC minutes Nov 18, PCE Nov 25, FOMC decision Dec 9, CPI Nov data Dec 10.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking because credit can flip, but nothing in the data yet says broad rollover: the index is holding its 200-day and credit is not cracking. The risk is treating a leadership rotation as a market top and de-risking the whole book on a Mag7 problem.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names sit 16.43% below their 52-week highs on average against SPY at 3.5% below its high, a 12.93-point divergence gap, and SPX itself is only 3.61% off its 120-day high (7,561.67 vs 7,844.52) while still 3.02% above its 200-day (7,340.32). Credit confirms the rotation read rather than a rollover: bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.2, calm. Rates are the binding constraint, not credit: the 10-year is 5.10%, the 2-year 4.86%, the real 10-year 2.86%.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a Mag7-led unwind: NVDA is 33.1% off its high and QQQ is 7.98% lower over one month while SPY is only 2.98% lower, which looks like the index leadership breaking.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4.0 or SPX closing below its 200-day at 7,340.32 — either would void the rotation read and confirm rollover.

themes.counterRead: The gap between price and fundamentals is the opportunity, but it is not yet a buy: NVDA sits BELOW its Zone 2 floor ($162.85 vs the $175-185 zone), SMH is inside Zone 2 ($486.75 vs $470-505) without a capitulation print, and the mechanical tally is only 2 of 4 (no volume climax, no VIX rollover). Fundamentals ahead of price is the setup; the trigger is still missing.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals moved the other way. NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year with the stock 33.1% below its high and RSI at 24.9 (oversold); AVGO revenue is up 55% with a 42.1% free-cash-flow margin; MU is $778.31, 38% below its high with RSI 42.5. Of the 14 FULL_SIGNAL dislocations, 11 are tagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN and only NVDA is ACUTE_CATALYST — the selloff is repricing sentiment, not reported demand.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure Washout
themes.narrative: The market has priced AI infrastructure as a busted trade: NVDA fell 12.75% in five days and 28.14% over one month, SMH is 27.55% off its high and below its 200-day, and the whole complex (PLTR -17.35% over one month, AVGO 29.9% off its high, LRCX 48.5% off its high) is being sold as if demand broke.
themes.watchFor: NVDA daily close back at or above $175 with SMH holding $470 — the zone reclaim that re-arms Tranche A.

themes.counterRead: The dislocation is the opportunity, but the entry is not armed: these are watchlist names, not buys, until the tape confirms. DDOG and ONTO are the board's top conviction scores (82 and 81), and the setup is fundamentals growing while prices fall — but a falling tape can keep falling, and the tally is still 2 of 4. The trigger is a zone reclaim plus a third tally signal, not the score alone.

themes.counterRead: VST at $133.01 is 29.7% below its high and the entry is still not armed — the data says the thesis is intact; the tape says wait for the level. Buying the narrative of a power supercycle without the level is chasing. Insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, but the price has not reclaimed its trend.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is the board's top conviction promotion (score 83): revenue is growing 19.1% year over year, free cash flow is $1,318M, P/S is 2.5x, and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. BWXT is 49.1% below its high with revenue growing 18.3% and positive free cash flow of $185M. The theme's decline is tagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN across the board, not a demand break. VST is a holding (18.04 shares), so this is a book position, not a new idea.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power

themes.watchFor: VST holding its trough with insider buying continuing, and a reclaim of its trend before any add is considered.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree here, which is itself the signal: this is de-leveraging, not indiscriminate selling. The names that held up are the ones with cash flow and real demand; the ones that fell are the ones that needed the story to keep running. That split is information, not noise — it says the tape is discriminating, which argues against blanket de-risking and for name-level triage.
themes.dataAnchor: The ranking of the damage is exactly what a leverage unwind looks like: the harder the leverage and the thinner the fundamental anchor, the deeper the fall — CONL -61.50% and TQQQ -25.36% against SPY -2.98% over one month; BTC -19.91%, IBIT -22.15%, ETH -22.54%, DOGE -25.00%, COIN -35.70%. Portfolio holdings sit in the blast radius: BMNR -30.61% over one month, DOGE -25.00%, CONL -61.50%. Meanwhile the unlevered, cash-generative leaders held up (MA +7.93% over one month, TMDX +18.94%, NXT +9.30%).
themes.label: Speculative Leverage Unwind
themes.narrative: The most-leveraged, most-narrative names fell hardest in the same tape: crypto and its proxies (BTC -19.91% in one month, ETH -22.54%, COIN -35.70%, IBIT -22.15%), leveraged single-stock ETFs (CONL -61.50%, TQQQ -25.36%) and story stocks (RDDT -39.95%, HIMS -35.33%) led the decline.
themes.watchFor: BTC-USD and CONL stabilizing after their -19.91% and -61.50% one-month slides while SPY holds its 200-day — a leverage unwind that stops spreading is the first sign the tape is finding a floor.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds at the NVDA $175 reclaim and the SMH $470 floor, and this week it is event-driven: FOMC minutes Nov 18 is the first catalyst, with PCE Nov 25 and the Dec 9 FOMC decision after it. SMH is already inside Zone 2 at $486.75 and NVDA is $12 below its zone floor, so the first confirmed zone reclaim plus a third tally signal is where the tape either bottoms or breaks to the next zone down.
